question.prompt: Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is a parallelogram, and \(E\) is the midpoint of the side \(\overline{AD}.\) Let \(F\) be the intersection of lines \(EB\) and \(AC.\) What is the ratio of the area of quadrilateral \(CDEF\) to the area of triangle \(CFB?\)

solutions.title: Use similarity and area ratios
solutions.explanation:
The midpoint condition gives \(AE=AD/2=CB/2\), suggesting a comparison of triangles \(AFE\) and \(CFB\).

Since \(AE\parallel CB\), we have \(\angle AEF=\angle CBF\). Also, \(\angle AFE=\angle CFB\) because they are vertical angles. Thus
\[
\triangle AFE\sim\triangle CFB.
\]
Their corresponding side ratio is \(AE:CB=1:2\), so \(FE:FB=1:2\), and their area ratio is \(1:4\).

Measure all areas in units of the area of \(\triangle AFE\). Then \(\triangle AFE\) has area \(1\), and \(\triangle CFB\) has area \(4\). Triangles \(AFE\) and \(AFB\) have bases \(FE\) and \(FB\) on the same line and share the altitude from \(A\). Their areas are therefore in the ratio \(1:2\), giving \(\triangle AFB\) area \(2\). Consequently, \(\triangle ABE\) has area \(1+2=3\).

Using \(AD\) as the parallelogram's base, \(\triangle ABE\) has half that base and the same height. The triangle area formula supplies another factor of \(1/2\), so its area is one-fourth of the parallelogram's area. Hence \(ABCD\) has area \(4\cdot3=12\).

Removing triangles \(AFE\), \(AFB\), and \(CFB\) leaves quadrilateral \(CDEF\), whose area is
\[
12-1-2-4=5.
\]
The requested ratio is \(\boxed{5:4}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
